# PAS-001 \- DocBridge Blueprint

**Blueprint: DocBridge, Batch File Distribution for Clinical Trial Documents**   
PAS-001 | Status: Draft | Owner: [Hayk Simonyan](mailto:hayk.simonyan.email@gmail.com) | Updated: 15.07.2026

## What problem we're solving and why

Clinical trial coordinators routinely need to place the same set of documents into many destinations at once. A typical case: 10 regulatory documents that must land in 15 team binders across 5 hospitals. Today that is 150 manual uploads, one file to one destination at a time.

**Current State:** The document platform only supports uploading a single file to a single destination. Coordinators repeat the same upload dozens or hundreds of times per batch. The work is slow, and because it is manual, files get skipped or land in the wrong binder with no record of what went wrong.

**Impact:** Coordinator hours are wasted on mechanical repetition. Worse, in a regulated clinical trial context, a missed or misplaced document is a compliance problem, not just an inconvenience. There is currently no way to answer "did every file reach every destination?" with confidence.

DocBridge is a standalone web application that solves this: select files once, map them to many destinations, submit as one batch, and track every individual delivery to a definitive success or failure: [DocBridge (Healthcare System)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-p6qBirF_B1tbUnb284egHBKmg-vrHdi6eDn6U-cKps/edit?tab=t.0)

## Definition of done

A user submits **N files × M destinations**; the system acknowledges instantly (does not block on processing), every file-to-destination pair is delivered asynchronously and independently, and the user can see per-destination status until the whole job resolves. No file is ever silently lost.

## Context

The client builds software for managing clinical trial documentation. DocBridge sits in front of the document platform, an electronic document management system organized as Team → Binder → Folder (optionally nested) → Document. Access is team-based: users only see and act on resources belonging to teams they are members of. The document platform runs in multiple geographic regions, and every delivery must be routed to the correct region for its destination.

Documents are organized into a hierarchy:  
Organization  
  └── Region (e.g. US, DE)  
        └── Team  
              └── Binder  
                    └── Folder (can be nested)  
                          └── Document  
There are no external systems. We build all three parts ourselves: the authentication capability, the document platform, and DocBridge.

### Key Terminologies

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| Document platform | The destination system. A permission-controlled document store organized as Team → Binder → Folder → Document, deployed per region. |
| Destination | A specific place a file can be delivered to: a binder or a folder within a binder, always belonging to a team. |
| Job | One batch submission. Contains the selected files and their destination mappings. |
| Task | One file-to-destination pair. The atomic unit of work. A job with 100 files and 20 destinations can contain up to 2,000 tasks. |
| Staging | Temporary encrypted storage where uploaded files live between submission and delivery. Staged files are retained 30 days after job completion, then deleted by lifecycle policy. |
| Delivery | The act of a worker transferring a staged file into the document platform at one destination, with integrity verified. |
| Task lifecycle | pending → in-progress → completed / failed. Pending: task created, message waiting in queue. In-progress: a worker owns it. |

### Assumptions

* The document platform is ours to build, so its ingestion API contract is ours to define. We will keep it minimal: authenticate, receive a file into a destination, confirm receipt.  
* A file is staged once and delivered many times. 100 files staged can produce up to 2,000 deliveries.  
* Team membership is the entire authorization model for v1. No per-document or per-folder permission overrides.  
* Users are trusted employees of client organizations, but the system must still enforce authorization on every operation. No operation runs unauthenticated.  
* "Region" is an attribute of a destination, known at destination-browsing time. Users do not choose regions; the system routes automatically.

## Job Stories

* When I start a distribution session, I want to browse only the teams, binders, and folders I actually have access to, so that I cannot target a destination I am not authorized for.  
* When I have a batch of documents to distribute, I want to select all files and map each to one or more destinations in a single session, so that I do not repeat the same upload dozens of times.  
* When I submit a batch, I want an immediate confirmation that the job was accepted, so that I can move on to other work while deliveries happen in the background.  
* When a job is running, I want to see the live status of every individual file-to-destination delivery, so that I know exactly what has landed and what is still pending.  
* When a delivery fails, I want to see which file, which destination, and why, so that I can fix the cause or escalate without guessing.  
* When a teammate has distributed documents, I want to download any file from their jobs, so that our team works from the same set of documents.

## High-Level Architecture

[https://app.eraser.io/workspace/Ojr9Ojf6NvEMgoqWsJMo?diagram=dHFSzsqF2iFy3v7TXelq](https://app.eraser.io/workspace/Ojr9Ojf6NvEMgoqWsJMo?origin=share&diagram=dHFSzsqF2iFy3v7TXelq) ![][image1]

Component Overview:

| Component | Responsibility |
| :---- | :---- |
| Web client (React SPA) | File selection, destination mapping, job submission, job/task dashboard. Uploads and downloads file bytes directly to/from the staging store using presigned URLs. |
| API Gateway | Single public entry point for all API traffic. Validates JWTs on every request before anything reaches the private network. Applies throttling. Never carries file bytes. |
| Internal ALB | Routes API traffic inside the private network to the right service by host/path rules. One ALB, one target group per service. Not reachable from the internet. |
| Auth service | User registration, login, credential storage, JWT issuance. The only component that handles passwords. |
| DocBridge API | Destination browsing (filtered by team membership), presigned URL issuance, job submission, job and task status queries. Owns the job/task records. Never touches file bytes. |
| Staging store (S3 \+ KMS) | Holds uploaded files encrypted at rest until deliveries complete. Enforces encryption on every write. 30-day retention after job completion via lifecycle policy. |
| Relational DB (PostgreSQL, one instance, three isolated logical databases) | Each service owns its data behind its own credentials: auth (users, credentials), platform (teams, memberships, hierarchy, documents), DocBridge (jobs, tasks, file metadata and checksums). No cross-service joins; cross-service data needs go through service APIs. Source of truth for job and task status. |
| Task queues (SQS \+ DLQs) | Two queues decouple submission from delivery: a job queue carries one fan-out message per submission, and a task queue carries one message per task. Fan-out absorbs the up-to-2,000-task spike outside the request path. Each queue has its own dead-letter queue so nothing is silently lost at either stage. |
| Worker tier (Lambda, SQS-triggered) | Two functions: fan-out (consumes job messages, batch-enqueues task messages) and delivery (fetches the staged file, verifies integrity, delivers to the document platform, updates task status, pushes the status change to subscribed WebSocket connections). Scales per message, to zero when idle. PostgreSQL access goes through RDS Proxy. |
| Document platform (mock DMS) | The destination system, one deployment per region. Receives files into binders/folders and confirms receipt. |

## User Flows

**Flow 1: Browse destinations**

1. User logs in and opens a new distribution session.  
2. Web client requests available regions from the auth service.  
3. Web client fetches teams (filtered to those with DocBridge enabled) from each region via DocBridge API.  
4. User expands a team to browse binders, then folders, lazy-loaded and filtered to what they're authorized to see.  
5. User selects one or more destinations for the batch.  
6. Expected outcome: user sees a permission-accurate destination tree in under 1 second, and cannot select anything outside their team access.

**Flow 2: Distribute a batch of documents**

1. User logs in and opens a new distribution session.  
2. User browses their available destinations (teams → binders → folders) and selects the targets for this batch.  
3. User selects up to 100 files. The browser uploads each file directly to the staging store; the UI shows per-file upload progress and stays responsive throughout.  
4. User maps files to destinations: any file to one or more destinations, any destination receiving one or more files.  
5. User submits. The system acknowledges immediately (under 500 ms) and shows the new job with all its tasks in pending state.  
6. In the background, each task is processed independently: the file is verified for integrity and delivered to the document platform in the correct region. Transient failures are retried automatically at least 3 times.  
7. Expected outcome: the job dashboard converges to a final state where every task is either completed or failed, with a reason attached to every failure. One task failing never blocks the others.

**Flow 3: Track a job**

1. User opens their job list and sees active and past jobs, each with an aggregate status derived from its tasks.  
2. User opens a job and sees every task: file, destination, current state (pending / in-progress / completed / failed).  
3. Statuses update automatically as workers progress; the user does not need to manually refresh.  
4. Expected outcome: the user can answer "did every file reach every destination?" at a glance, and for any failure, see which file, which destination, and what went wrong.

**Flow 4: Retrieve a file**

1. User opens a job submitted by any member of their teams.  
2. User picks a file and requests a download.  
3. The system authorizes the request against team membership and hands the browser a direct, time-limited download from the staging store. File bytes never pass through application servers.  
4. Expected outcome: authorized team members can retrieve any staged file from their teams' jobs; nobody else can, at any point in the pipeline.

## Technical Design

Technical Design Document (TDD): to be written after this blueprint is approved. All schemas, API contracts, task estimates, concurrency and failure analysis, edge cases, and the launch plan live there.

## Releases

### Release 1: Core pipeline

Target Date: TBD | Status: Planned | Total Estimate: \[from TDD\]

**Scope (feature level):**

* User registration, login, and token-based sessions  
* Destination browsing filtered by real team membership  
* Multi-file selection with direct-to-staging upload and per-file progress  
* File-to-destination mapping and one-action batch submission with instant acknowledgment  
* Asynchronous, independent per-task delivery with automatic retries  
* Job and task status tracking down to individual failure reasons  
* Team-scoped file download, direct from staging  
* Encrypted staging with 30-day post-completion retention

**Dependencies:**

* None external. Auth service and document platform are built as part of this release.

**Success Metrics:**

| Metric | Target | How we measure |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Job submission latency | p99 \< 500 ms regardless of batch size | Submission API response time |
| No silent file loss | 0 undetected failures | Every failed task surfaces in the status view; DLQ depth stays at 0 under normal ops |
| Delivery failure rate | ≤ 0.1% under normal conditions | Failed tasks / total tasks over a rolling window |
| Destination browser load time | \< 1 s for users with ≤ 50 teams | Time to interactive on first browse |
| Partial failure isolation | Failed task does not block siblings | Integration test: kill one delivery, assert others complete |
| End-to-end pipeline | Full batch completes in local and cloud environments | Smoke test: N files × M destinations → all tasks DONE |

**Risks:**

* Fan-out spike: a single submission creating 2,000 tasks could overwhelm downstream processing | Mitigation: queue absorbs the spike; workers scale horizontally and pull at their own pace  
* Duplicate deliveries: queue redelivery could deliver the same file twice to the same destination | Mitigation: workers and the document platform treat delivery as idempotent per task  
* Client-reported uploads: a submitted job could reference a file that never finished uploading | Mitigation: verify object existence and checksum before delivery; surface a clear task failure otherwise

### Release 2: Operational maturity

Target Date: TBD | Status: Planned

High-level only; details after Release 1 learnings. 

Candidate themes: 

* Multi-region routing per destination  
* job cancellation  
* re-run of failed tasks in one action  
* richer delivery reporting (per-destination summaries, export)  
* edge throttling tuned per client organization  
* push-based live status if polling proves too chatty.  
* Structured logging with correlation IDs across all services  
* Advanced per-binder role-based access control
